definition.text: Human is the door where a person submits work directly and drives it live. This repo's own target architecture states the requirement as the first of its entry kinds: "A human must be able to enter the system." The worked reference example spells out what that means operationally for this specific door: a person submits it, the gate asks live, and the resulting card lands in the terminal.

evidence.quote: A human must be able to enter the system.
What the gate does | asks, live
Where the card goes | the terminal

standards.role: the event contract between an agent and a person's rendered UI surface -- a typed, bidirectional event stream standardising how an agent connects to a user-facing frontend once a human is looking at one.
standards.covers: does not cover a bare CLI invocation or a programmatic API call with no UI attached, and does not cover a coding-editor session -- that is the Agent Client Protocol's territory, and this repo's own capability table assigns ACP to the Agent runtime / Harness card (3.1), not to this one (see gaps).

evidence.text: AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.

evidence.quote: AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.
it standardizes how agent state, UI intents, and user interactions flow between your model/agent runtime and user-facing frontend applications

landscape.text: This repo's own proposed synthesis: no single standard covers the whole "UI / CLI / API" sub-line this card carries. AG-UI standardises only the UI slice -- a typed event stream from an agent to a rendered frontend -- and says nothing about a bare CLI invocation or a programmatic API call with no UI attached. The Agent Client Protocol standardises a narrower, adjacent thing again: an editor-to-coding-agent session (open a session, prompt, stream, cancel, stop reason), which this repo's own capability table already assigns to the Agent runtime / Harness card, not to a general human front door. A third shape, MCP elicitation, is narrower still: one tool pausing mid-run for one structured answer, not an entry point at all. The real tradeoff is between a UI-native protocol built to watch and steer a running agent (AG-UI) and a session/turn protocol built to run a coding agent (ACP) -- badging one card with the wrong half of that pair conflates "how a human enters" with "how a human's editor drives a coding agent."

usage.text: A caller enters through this door by submitting work directly and staying present for it: the reference model's own comparison table says of this door specifically that "a person submits it," that the identity of record is "the person," that when the run needs a decision the gate "asks, live," and that the response artifact lands in "the terminal." That is a synchronous, present caller -- the mirror image of the Scheduled door's queued, absentee owner.

gaps.what: reference-model.json badges this card with ACP, but this repo's own sourced capability table assigns Agent Client Protocol to a different capability entirely: "Agent runtime," adapter today goose -- exactly the Harness card (3.1), not an entry door. Every ACP-specific research record gathered for this repo (cap-agent-runtime and litmus-a lenses) independently describes it the same way: an editor-to-coding-agent session, local or remote, not a general UI/CLI/API front door.
gaps.why_it_matters: a caller reading this card for "what protocol do I speak to enter as a human" is pointed at a coding-agent session protocol that a CLI script or a bare API POST cannot use, and the same badge appearing on both this card and (properly) on Harness means the badge does no distinguishing work across the two.
gaps.research_query: should reference-model.json's badge for card 1.1 be corrected from ACP to AG-UI, leaving ACP only on 3.1 Harness?

gaps.what: AG-UI is the better-evidenced fit for this card, but it is not in this repo's own adopted capability table -- PASS.md's B3 list (the middle column this repo treats as authoritative) has no "Human interaction" / UI-entry row at all, sourced or otherwise. AG-UI's placement here rests entirely on search-only research (X-cap-human-interaction-001, X-entry-composition-020), never fetched with capture.py, never ratified by an owner decision record.
gaps.why_it_matters: swapping the badge from ACP to AG-UI would fix the misplacement this brief flagged, but it would still trade one weak, wrong badge for a better-argued, unconfirmed one -- this card's "built" status is not backed by an owner-adopted standard the way, e.g., Isolation's OCI Runtime Spec is.
gaps.research_query: capture.py the AG-UI spec directly and add a Human-interaction / UI-entry row to PASS.md's B3 table if the owner adopts it

gaps.what: no standard found in this repo's evidence covers the CLI or API thirds of this card's own sub-line ("UI / CLI / API") -- AG-UI covers only the UI third; the closest CLI/API evidence is the generic, unnamed "CLI" adapter entry in F-b3-08 and RFC 9457/idempotency-key conventions that apply to the API transport layer generally, not to human entry specifically.
gaps.why_it_matters: a card whose sub-line promises three surfaces but whose standards array can only evidence one overstates how settled this door is.
gaps.research_query: is there a standard entry contract for CLI or bare-API human submission distinct from a UI event stream
